swedbank.name: Swedbank
swedbank.insurer: Swedbank Life Insurance SE, Lithuanian branch
swedbank.overview:
Term life insurance with no savings component; it can be linked to a loan agreement, in which case the sum insured equals the outstanding loan unless the policy states otherwise.
The additional severe disability cover is included in the contract unless the policy says otherwise; an accident injury cover can be added on top.
Valid around the clock, worldwide.
Premiums are monthly; the insurer may change the premium unilaterally when the statistical mortality, injury or incapacity risk changes.
An optional automatic yearly increase of the sum insured (on the insured person's birthday).
LI2020 allows cancellation with a full refund within 30 calendar days of concluding the contract. The pre-contractual sheet instead counts from delivery of the policy; confirm the applicable deadline. A payout decision is due within 30 calendar days after the circumstances are established and all required documents received; an official proceeding can delay the decision.
The supplied pre-contractual information describes premiums as ineligible for income tax relief and insured-event benefits as tax exempt; taxation depends on the applicable law at payment.
The rules state no entry age limits or contract term – these are set in the contract.
Unpaid premiums can suspend all cover after the additional payment deadline; events during suspension are not covered. Cover resumes the day after the debt is paid. Disclose requested health information and increases in occupational or hobby risk; omissions can reduce or prevent a payout. Sanctions can also end cover.
Report claims as soon as possible and provide the requested evidence.

life.product: Gyvybės draudimas / Gyvybės draudimas paskolos grąžinimui (rules No. LI2020)
life.summary: A lump-sum life insurance payout to the beneficiary when the insured person dies.
life.event: Death of the insured person while the cover is in force – from illness or from an accident.
life.payout:
The life sum insured in force on the day of the event.
If the contract is linked to a loan – additionally the loan interest for up to 2 months after the event; if the life sum insured is smaller than the outstanding loan, that interest is reduced proportionally.
A severe disability payout made earlier reduces the life sum insured.
life.terms:
The term and the sum insured are set in the contract; the rules state no age limits.
A loan-linked contract ends when the loan is repaid.
Life cover starts on the contract date; for a loan-linked contract it starts the next working day, no earlier than disbursement of the loan or part of it.
life.exclusions:
Suicide within the first 3 years of the contract.
Driving a vehicle under the influence of alcohol or other substances.
Flying activities, piloting an aircraft or flying as a crew member (scheduled passenger flights are covered).
Nuclear accident, weapons of mass destruction, military action (taking part in military exercises is covered).
Intentional criminal activity.
On uninterrupted replacement of a previous life policy, the suicide period counts from the previous policy’s start, with the payout capped by both sums until the new policy has run for 3 years. An increase in the life sum is excluded for suicide within 3 years of that increase.

accidentalDeath.summary: No separate cover. Accidental death is covered by the general life insurance, with no extra sum paid for it.

criticalIllness.summary: No critical illness cover is specified in the reviewed Swedbank policies.

cancer.summary: No cancer cover is specified in the reviewed Swedbank policies.

childCriticalIllness.summary: No children’s critical illness cover is specified in the reviewed Swedbank policies.

disability.product: Papildomas sunkios negalios draudimas (rules No. DI2020)
disability.summary: A payout if illness or an accident leaves the insured person with a participation level of 30 % or less.
disability.event:
Severe disability: a participation level of 30 % or less established by the competent Lithuanian authority and lasting continuously for 12 months or longer.
The definition also requires a significant loss of physical or mental abilities limiting any work or self-care. Consecutive 6-month assessment periods may be combined, with gaps of no more than 30 calendar days. The event date is the date from which the authority establishes the qualifying level.
disability.payout:
Equal to the life sum insured on the day of the event unless agreed otherwise; for a loan-linked contract also up to 2 months of loan interest.
After the payout this cover ends and the life sum insured is reduced by the amount paid (when it reaches zero, the life insurance ends too).
Loan interest is reduced proportionally if the life sum is below the loan balance. The pre-contractual information says disability is considered first when both death and disability claims are made, with their combined benefit capped at the life sum; no disability benefit follows an already-paid life benefit.
disability.terms:
Valid until the day before the insured person turns 60.
No separate initial waiting period is stated; the 12-month disability requirement still applies.
The cover runs in 12-month periods and renews automatically; the insurer may change the terms and the premium from the start of each new period.
disability.exclusions:
Intentional self-harm or attempted suicide.
Driving under the influence of alcohol or other substances.
Flying activities (scheduled passenger flights are covered).
Nuclear accident, military action (military exercises are covered).
Intentional criminal activity.

accidentDisability.summary: No separate cover. Lasting consequences of an injury are covered only as far as they meet the severe disability definition (participation of 30 % or less); in the injury cover a limb amputation is paid as a bone fracture.

injuries.product: Papildomas traumų dėl nelaimingų atsitikimų draudimas (rules No. TR2020)
injuries.summary: Fixed payouts in euros for the injuries listed in the table; the sum insured is the same for everyone – 20 000 EUR per insurance period.
injuries.event:
A sudden, unexpected accident caused by external factors that results in an injury listed in the injury table.
A doctor must be seen within 48 hours.
Fractures require radiologist confirmation; otherwise the bruise benefit applies. Full dislocations require a reduction procedure.
injuries.payout:
Fixed amounts, for example: femur fracture – 3 000 EUR, humerus fracture – 2 000 EUR, joint dislocation (fingers and toes excluded) – 600 EUR, nasal bone fracture – 400 EUR, mild brain injury – 200 EUR.
Additionally, only alongside another injury benefit: 150 EUR per inpatient day within 90 days of the accident, excluding rehabilitation and nursing; 600 EUR per event for open surgery or arthroscopy within 180 days. Repeat surgery, closed reduction and surgical wound treatment do not qualify for another surgery benefit.
No more than 20 000 EUR per 12-month period; once the full sum is paid the cover ends.
If the insured person dies within 10 days of the event and as a result of it, only the life insurance payout is made.
Minor fractures under table item 20 pay 400 EUR per bone, capped at 1 600 EUR, instead of the usual fracture benefit. Multiple breaks of one bone count once. A fracture benefit cannot be combined with dislocation or related soft-tissue benefits in the same area; a dislocation benefit likewise excludes related soft-tissue benefits.
Item 19 injuries pay 400 EUR (group a) or 200 EUR (group b, only without a group-a injury), for at most two events per insurance period.
injuries.terms:
Valid until the day before the insured person turns 70.
The cover runs in 12-month periods and renews automatically; it can be dropped at any time while keeping the life insurance.
Cover starts the day after concluding the life contract or approval of adding this cover; loan-linked cover cannot start before loan disbursement. Renewal terms and premiums can change; additional costs or obligations require at least 30 calendar days’ notice.
injuries.exclusions:
Illnesses, degenerative processes, inflammations and infections; intervertebral disc and meniscus damage, hernias, dental injuries, frostbite.
Intoxication of 2 per mille or more, or under the influence of drugs; driving under the influence.
Professional sport and motor vehicle sport (recreational riding is covered).
Climbing and hiking above 4 500 m, diving deeper than 40 m, flying activities.
Military action, nuclear accident, intentional criminal activity, consequences of treatment or surgery.
Attempted suicide, intentional self-harm and recurrent dislocations or joint instability. The aviation exclusion has an exception for scheduled passenger flights; the military exclusion has an exception for military exercises.
injuries.references: TR2020, pp. 1–6, especially table items 19–22 and additional payment conditions.

dailyAllowance.summary: No daily allowance – injury payouts do not depend on the length of sick leave or lost income.

hospitalAllowance.product: Part of the accident injury insurance
hospitalAllowance.summary: No separate hospital allowance, but the injury cover pays for a hospital stay after an accident.
hospitalAllowance.event: Inpatient treatment (excluding rehabilitation and nursing) within 90 days of an insured accident.
hospitalAllowance.payout: 150 EUR per day spent in hospital; paid only on top of another injury payout and within the overall 20 000 EUR sum.
hospitalAllowance.terms: Same as the injury cover: ends the day before age 70 and depends on the life cover remaining in force.
hospitalAllowance.exclusions:
A hospital stay because of illness is not covered.
All exclusions of the injury cover apply.

medicalExpenses.summary: Medical expenses are not reimbursed – injury payouts do not depend on the treatment costs incurred.

seb.name: SEB
seb.insurer: SEB Life and Pension Baltic SE
seb.overview:
Personal insurance is assembled from covers chosen one by one; each has its own rules and its own sum insured stated in the policy.
All rules are effective from 2026-02-26 and apply together with SEB's Personal insurance rules. The general terms (premiums, cancellation, payout deadlines) are in that document, which is not among the sources here.
People aged 18–68 can be insured and the covers end at 70; for critical illness and permanent incapacity cover the limits are 18–63 and 65.
Dangerous hobbies, voluntary work in defence organisations, rescue work or firefighting, and professional sport are covered only if included in the contract (this exclusion does not apply to the life cover).
The critical illness and incapacity payout can be reduced or refused if the insured person lived outside the EU and EFTA for more than 13 consecutive weeks in the 12 months before the event.
Requested information must be accurate and complete; information related to a claim can affect payment. The reviewed risk rules do not establish the full claims procedure or general contract terms because the Personal insurance rules are missing.

documents.disabilityRules: Permanent incapacity for work insurance rules (in Lithuanian)

life.summary: When the insured person dies, the sum insured is paid to the people they chose.
life.event: Death of the insured person while the cover is in force.
life.payout: The sum stated in the policy – to the beneficiaries named in the contract or to the heirs.
life.terms:
Aged 18 to 68 at the start of the insurance.
The cover ends at the age of 70.
life.exclusions:
Suicide within the first 2 years of the cover or of an increase of the sum insured.
Operating a vehicle, vessel or aircraft above the legal limits for alcohol or other substances.
Radioactive radiation.
War, civil war, rebellion, terrorism, revolution, taking part in mass unrest.
Intentional unlawful acts. Knowingly false or incomplete requested information related to the insured event may lead to a reduced or refused payout.

accidentalDeath.product: Draudimas nuo mirties dėl nelaimingo atsitikimo
accidentalDeath.summary: An extra sum if death is caused by an accident.
accidentalDeath.event: Death caused by an accident (including heat stroke and poisoning), occurring no later than one year after it.
accidentalDeath.payout: The sum stated in the policy – to the beneficiaries or the heirs.
accidentalDeath.terms:
Aged 18 to 68 at the start of the insurance.
The cover ends at the age of 70.
accidentalDeath.exclusions:
Suicide; illness, disability or mental disorder.
Use of alcohol, drugs or toxic substances; ignoring a doctor's instructions.
Infection (except tetanus and rabies); treatment or surgery not performed because of the accident.
War, terrorism, mass unrest, radioactive radiation, intentional unlawful acts.
Dangerous hobbies, voluntary defence or rescue work and professional sport not included in the contract.
These exclusions concern what caused the death or injury; having an unrelated illness or disability is not itself listed as a blanket exclusion.

criticalIllness.summary: A lump sum on the first diagnosis of one of 15 life-threatening illnesses.
criticalIllness.event:
First diagnosis of one of 15 conditions: malignant tumour (cancer), myocardial infarction, stroke, kidney failure, heart and vascular surgery (bypass, aorta, valves), severe bacterial meningitis or encephalitis, benign brain tumour, major organ transplant, multiple sclerosis, Parkinson's disease before 60, advanced dementia before 60, loss of hearing, speech or sight due to illness, loss of limbs or paralysis due to illness.
A diagnosis name alone is insufficient: all disease-specific criteria must be met. Examples include persistent heart dysfunction after infarction, permanent neurological deficit assessed at least 3 months after stroke, and multiple sclerosis causing inability to walk 200 m unaided or eat independently.
criticalIllness.payout:
The full sum stated in the policy – to the insured person.
The cover ends when the insured event occurs.
criticalIllness.terms:
Aged 18 to 63 at the start; the cover ends at the age of 65.
Waiting period – 90 days from the start of the cover; after an increase of the sum insured it applies again, but only to the increased part.
criticalIllness.exclusions:
Death within one month of the insured event.
Early-stage cancer, transient ischaemic attacks and the other exceptions listed in each illness definition.
HIV or AIDS; use of alcohol or drugs; self-harm; ignoring a doctor's instructions.
War, terrorism, radioactive radiation, intentional unlawful acts.
Dangerous hobbies and professional sport not included in the contract; a long stay outside the EU and EFTA.
For residence outside the EU/EFTA, the threshold is more than 13 consecutive weeks in the 12 months before the event; the insurer may reduce or refuse payment. Undeclared voluntary defence, rescue or firefighting activities can also lead to reduction or refusal.
criticalIllness.references: Critical illness rules, pp. 1–5, definitions 1–15, waiting period and exclusions.

cancer.product: Part of the critical illness insurance
cancer.summary: No separate cancer insurance – a malignant tumour is one of the 15 critical illnesses.
cancer.event: A malignant tumour confirmed by histology or cytology.
cancer.payout: The full critical illness sum insured; there are no partial payouts for early-stage cancer.
cancer.terms:
As for the critical illness cover: aged 18–63 at the start, until 65, a 90-day waiting period.
After a sum increase, the 90-day waiting period applies only to the increased portion. Cover ends on the insured event.
cancer.exclusions:
Cancer in situ, cervical dysplasia, pre-cancerous and non-invasive conditions.
Early-stage melanoma (below T2N0M0) and other skin tumours without metastases.
Papillary thyroid carcinoma or prostate cancer staged below T2N0M0.
Stage 1 Hodgkin or non-Hodgkin lymphoma; leukaemia that has not caused anaemia.
All critical illness exclusions apply, including death within one month of the event and the residence restriction outside the EU/EFTA.

childCriticalIllness.summary: No children’s critical illness cover is specified in these SEB policies; the reviewed covers start at age 18.

disability.summary: A payout if illness or an accident leaves the insured person permanently unable to work.
disability.event: Permanent loss of capacity for work: a participation level of no more than 30 %, officially established by the competent Lithuanian authority for a continuous period of at least 12 months.
disability.payout:
The sum stated in the policy – to the insured person.
The cover ends when the insured event occurs.
disability.terms:
Aged 18 to 63 at the start; the cover ends at the age of 65.
Waiting period – 90 days (not applied in the case of an accident).
The 90-day period also applies after increasing the sum, but only to the increase.
disability.exclusions:
Self-harm or attempted suicide; ignoring a doctor's instructions.
Use of alcohol, drugs or toxic substances; driving under the influence.
War, terrorism, mass unrest, radioactive radiation, intentional unlawful acts.
Dangerous hobbies, voluntary defence or rescue work and professional sport not included in the contract.
Living outside the EU and EFTA for more than 13 consecutive weeks in the 12 months before the event – the payout can be reduced or refused.

accidentDisability.summary: A payout for incurable lasting consequences of an accident – as a percentage of the sum insured.
accidentDisability.event: A lasting functional impairment or the loss of a body part or sense organ caused by an accident and lasting longer than one year.
accidentDisability.payout:
A percentage of the sum insured according to the table, for example: quadriplegia or a severe head injury with a coma of at least 96 hours and residual neurological damage – 100 %, loss of an arm above the elbow or a leg above the knee – 70 %, loss of sight in one eye – 50 %, loss of the spleen – 10 %.
A partial loss of function is assessed proportionally; a payout below 1 % is not made.
An impairment not listed in the table is covered if participation dropped by more than 25 %.
Injuries to several body parts add up to at most 100 % of the sum insured.
Pre-existing functional impairment reduces the benefit. For the 100 % severe-head-injury example, life support throughout the coma and a Glasgow score of 3–8 are also required.
accidentDisability.terms:
Aged 18 to 68 at the start of the insurance.
The cover ends at the age of 70 or once 100 % of the sum insured has been paid.
accidentDisability.exclusions:
Illness, disability, mental disorder; chronic, inflammatory and age-related conditions (hernias, arthritis, tendinitis and others).
Self-harm; use of alcohol or drugs; driving under the influence.
Infection (except tetanus and rabies); treatment or surgery not performed because of the accident.
War, terrorism, radioactive radiation, intentional unlawful acts.
Dangerous hobbies, voluntary defence or rescue work and professional sport not included in the contract.
These exclusions concern what caused the death or injury; having an unrelated illness or disability is not itself listed as a blanket exclusion.

injuries.summary: A payout for fractures, dislocations, tears and other injuries – as a percentage of the chosen sum insured.
injuries.event:
A physical injury caused by an accident (including heat stroke and poisoning) while the cover is in force.
A fracture or dislocation must be clearly visible on an X-ray or CT; absent examination or signs of a new injury, payment can be reduced or refused.
injuries.payout:
A percentage of the sum insured according to the injury table, for example: femur fracture or brain concussion – 15 %, humerus fracture – 10 %, knee meniscus tear – 2 %, nasal bone fracture – 2 %, stitched wounds, burns of the second degree or higher and frostbite – 1.5 %.
An additional 3 % for a hospital stay of at least 3 consecutive bed-days and for each surgery within one year (several surgeries during the same hospital stay count as one; stitching a wound or a closed fracture reduction does not count as surgery).
An injury not listed in the table that needs at least 10 days of treatment – 0.4 % (once per insurance year).
No more than 100 % of the sum insured per insurance year.
For several injuries to the same body part in one accident, only the highest percentage is paid. Repeat soft-tissue injuries around the same joint during one insurance year are paid only for the first event.
injuries.terms:
Aged 18 to 68 at the start of the insurance.
The cover ends at the age of 70.
injuries.exclusions:
Illness, disability, mental disorder; recurring dislocations; chronic and inflammatory conditions (hernias, arthritis, tendinitis, bursitis and others).
Self-harm; use of alcohol or drugs; driving under the influence.
Infection (except tetanus and rabies); treatment or surgery not performed because of the accident.
War, terrorism, radioactive radiation, intentional unlawful acts.
Dangerous hobbies, voluntary defence or rescue work and professional sport not included in the contract.
These exclusions concern what caused the death or injury; having an unrelated illness or disability is not itself listed as a blanket exclusion.

dailyAllowance.summary: No daily allowance for temporary incapacity is specified in the reviewed SEB policies.

hospitalAllowance.summary: No separate hospital allowance, but the injury insurance pays a supplement for a hospital stay.
hospitalAllowance.event: A hospital stay of at least 3 consecutive bed-days because of an insured injury.
hospitalAllowance.payout:
A one-off supplement of 3 % of the injury sum insured; nothing is paid per day.
The supplement counts towards the injury cover’s overall limit of 100 % of the sum per insurance year.
hospitalAllowance.terms: As for the injury insurance: aged 18–68 at the start, until 70.
hospitalAllowance.exclusions:
A hospital stay because of illness is not covered.
All exclusions of the injury insurance apply.

medicalExpenses.summary: No reimbursement of medical expenses is specified in the reviewed SEB policies.

ergo.name: ERGO
ergo.overview:
Term life insurance with no savings component under general rules No. 028; one contract can insure several people (a family), and the policyholder can be a company.
The covers are chosen one by one: life, cancer, critical illness for adults and for children, accidents, total loss of capacity for work.
Age at the start of the insurance: 0–74 for life cover, 0–69 for accident cover, 18–64 for adult critical illness, 2–17 for children, 18–64 for loss of capacity for work.
Minimum life sum insured – 3 000 EUR; for cancer, critical illness and loss of capacity for work – 10 000 EUR. Minimum term – 5 years (1 year for group insurance).
Premiums are yearly, half-yearly, quarterly or monthly; the cover starts only once the first premium is received. If a debt is not settled within 30 days of a notice, the cover can be suspended, and after 6 months of suspension the contract can be terminated.
An individual policyholder can withdraw within 30 days of being informed that the contract was concluded, with a full refund; payouts are made within 30 days of receiving all the information.
The supplied pre-contractual information describes premiums as ineligible for income tax relief and insured-event benefits as tax exempt; taxation depends on the applicable law at payment.
The accident cover is valid around the clock, worldwide.
A price list for additional contract administration services applies.
The insurer can set different minimum sums or terms. Benefits require the selected risks to appear in the policy. Claims must normally be reported in writing within 30 days of the relevant injury, diagnosis, disability determination or death. Disclose requested health information and changes in risk.
Cover cannot precede the agreed start. A late first premium starts cover only the following day; general clause 3.2.2 provides limited retrospective cover when a later first-payment date was agreed and met.
The general rules count the 30-day withdrawal period from policy delivery, while the newer pre-contractual sheet counts from notification of conclusion; confirm the applicable deadline. Later cancellation normally refunds the unused premium. Sanctions may restrict cover or terminate the contract.
The definitions of professional and extreme sport matter: federation competitions can count as professional sport, while specified recreational activities are excepted (for example piste skiing and recreational diving to 40 m). Consult general §§1.21–1.22 for the activity and supervision conditions.
The supplied price list charges 0 EUR for changing the contract. The insurer can change terms only under the rules’ stated grounds and notice requirements; some special conditions allow changes with at least 30 days’ notice.

documents.rules: General rules No. 028, special conditions, price list and pre-contractual information (Lithuanian; pre-contractual information effective 2026-06-19; individual sections have earlier effective dates)

life.summary: When the insured person dies, the life sum insured is paid to the beneficiaries or heirs.
life.event:
Death of the insured person while the cover is in force; also a court decision declaring the insured person dead.
For a court declaration, the established date of death must fall within cover; a declaration that someone is missing is insufficient.
life.payout:
The sum insured in force at the time of death (it can be a changing sum).
If no beneficiary is named, the payout goes to the heirs.
For suicide within 3 years of a sum increase, outside the initial exclusion period, the benefit is the lowest sum insured in the previous 3 years.
life.terms:
Aged 0 to 74 at the start of the insurance.
Minimum sum insured – 3 000 EUR, minimum term – 5 years.
The insurer may set other minimums; the stated minimum term is 1 year for group insurance.
life.exclusions:
Suicide within the first 3 years of the cover.
Military action, a state of war or emergency, internal unrest.
Effects of nuclear energy.
Criminal acts of the insured person (stated in the pre-contractual information).
life.references: 028-02 §§3–7; printed pp. 18–19. General terms and pre-contractual information also apply.

accidentalDeath.product: Mirtis dėl nelaimingo atsitikimo (special conditions No. 028-03)
accidentalDeath.summary: An extra sum if the insured person dies because of an accident.
accidentalDeath.event: Death from injuries sustained in an accident within one year of it; also a court decision declaring the person dead when they are presumed to have died in an insured event.
accidentalDeath.payout:
The accidental death sum stated in the policy.
Disability and injury payouts already made for the same event are deducted from it.
accidentalDeath.terms:
Aged 0 to 69 at the start of the insurance.
Valid around the clock, worldwide.
accidentalDeath.exclusions:
Suicide; death from illness.
Acts incurring criminal or administrative liability; taking part in a fight.
Poisoning by alcohol, narcotic or psychotropic substances.
Acts of war, military missions, riots, nuclear energy and radiation.
Professional and extreme sport or leisure unless agreed otherwise (does not apply to insured persons under 18).
The fighting exclusion excepts necessary self-defence, performance of official duties and other socially valuable actions.
Moderate/severe intoxication excludes an accident only when it influenced the event; poisoning by alcohol or the other specified substances is separately excluded.
accidentalDeath.references: 028-03 §§3, 4.1, 5; printed pp. 20–21, 26. General terms and pre-contractual information also apply.

criticalIllness.product: Suaugusių asmenų draudimas nuo vėžio ir kitų kritinių ligų (special conditions No. 028-04)
criticalIllness.summary:
Three variants to choose from: A – cancer only, B – 4 critical illnesses, C – 39 critical illnesses.
The adult cover also includes cancer protection for minor children and adopted children; this does not give them the adult’s full critical illness list.
criticalIllness.event:
First diagnosis, while the cover is in force, of an illness or surgery on the chosen list.
Variant B: cancer, myocardial infarction, stroke, multiple sclerosis.
Variant C additionally includes bypass, valve and aorta surgery, kidney and liver failure, paralysis, blindness, deafness, loss of speech, Parkinson's disease, coma, benign brain tumour, severe head injury, loss of limbs, third-degree burns, bacterial meningitis and other illnesses.
Each illness must meet the detailed criteria in appendix 1; the number of illnesses alone does not show the breadth of cover.
criticalIllness.payout:
The full critical illness sum insured – to the insured person; the cover ends once it is paid.
For cancer, partial payouts (10 % or 20 % of the sum) are also possible and are not deducted from a later 100 % payout.
For the included children’s cancer cover, see the cancer card for the half-sum/per-parent limits and dependency on the parent’s cover.
criticalIllness.terms:
Aged 18 to 64 at the start; the cover lasts until the age of 70 at most.
Waiting period – generally 3 months; see the cancer qualification below; it does not apply to consequences of an accident – blindness, paralysis, loss of limbs, deafness, coma, severe head injury.
Minimum sum insured – 10 000 EUR.
Clause 028-04 §4.1.1 states 3 months, including after reinstatement; the pre-contractual sheet and separate cancer conditions state 6 months for cancer (3 for employee groups unless otherwise agreed). Confirm the cancer waiting period in the policy. The specified accident exceptions and uninterrupted continuation of equivalent ERGO cover can waive the 3-month restriction.
For illness within 3 months of a sum increase, §6.5 uses the sum from 3 months earlier, except the listed accident consequences.
criticalIllness.exclusions:
Death from the critical illness within 30 days of the diagnosis (does not apply to cancer).
HIV or AIDS.
Effects of alcohol, narcotic or psychotropic substances; intentional self-harm.
Acts of war, peacekeeping missions, nuclear energy and radioactive radiation; criminal acts.
Professional and extreme sport or leisure unless the insurer accepted this risk in the contract.
The radioactive-radiation exclusion excepts the consequences of radiotherapy.
criticalIllness.references: 028-04 §§2–6, appendix 1; printed pp. 50–60. General terms and pre-contractual information also apply.

cancer.summary: A separate cancer cover with partial payouts for early-stage cancer; the insured person's minor children are covered automatically.
cancer.event: Cancer confirmed by histology and diagnosed by an oncologist, haematologist or pathologist: invasive, invasive skin or non-invasive (early-stage).
cancer.payout:
100 % for invasive cancer meeting §3.3.2; 20 % for the specified non-invasive/early cancers; 10 % only for the listed invasive skin cancers (basal-cell, squamous-cell carcinoma and dermatofibrosarcoma). Each partial benefit is paid once per person.
Early prostate cancer qualifies for 20 % only at T1aN0M0, T1bN0M0 or T2aN0M0 with radical prostatectomy; early papillary/follicular thyroid cancer must be T1. Other exclusions and staging criteria in §3 apply.
A minor child’s sum is half the insured parent’s sum, capped at 25 000 EUR per parent; when both parents are insured, their contributions are combined under §§5.2–5.3.
An invasive-cancer payout ends the adult’s cover and the associated children’s cover.
cancer.terms:
Aged 18 to 64 at the start; the cover lasts until the age of 70 at most, for children until 18.
Waiting period – 6 months (3 months for employee group insurance); if cancer is diagnosed during it and the premium-paying insured person can no longer be insured, their premiums are refunded and their cover ends.
Minimum sum insured – 10 000 EUR.
Within 6 months of a sum increase (3 for employee groups unless agreed otherwise), the earlier sum applies. Children’s cover depends on a parent’s cancer cover remaining in force.
cancer.exclusions:
Tumours diagnosed before the contract and the listed pre-cancerous conditions (changed moles, colon polyposis, Crohn's disease, ulcerative colitis, hepatitis, liver cirrhosis and others), including prior diagnostic consultations. The exception requires no disease found or recovery after remission, written medical evidence supplied before contracting, and the insurer accepting the contract with full information.
A diagnosis based only on tumour markers in body fluids.
HIV or AIDS.
Effects of alcohol, narcotic or psychotropic substances.
Acts of war, nuclear energy, radioactive radiation.
cancer.references: 028-01 §§2–5; printed pp. 15–17. General terms and pre-contractual information also apply.

childCriticalIllness.product: Vaikų draudimas nuo vėžio ir kitų kritinių ligų (special conditions No. 028-05)
childCriticalIllness.summary: A separate cover for children against a list of 14 critical illnesses.
childCriticalIllness.event:
First diagnosis of one of 14 conditions, among them: cancer, organ or bone marrow transplant, chronic kidney failure, paralysis of limbs, blindness, coma, acute viral encephalitis, severe head injury, loss of limbs, bacterial meningitis, type 1 diabetes.
All condition-specific diagnostic and severity criteria in appendix 1 must be met.
childCriticalIllness.payout:
The full critical illness sum insured; the cover ends once it is paid.
For cancer, partial payouts too: 20 % for non-invasive or early-stage cancer, 10 % for invasive skin cancer.
Earlier partial cancer benefits are not deducted from a subsequent 100 % benefit.
childCriticalIllness.terms:
Aged 2 to 17 at the start; the cover lasts until the age of 18 at most.
Waiting period – 3 months.
The 3-month period also applies after reinstatement. Exceptions include written agreement, uninterrupted continuation of equivalent ERGO cover and the specified accident consequences. A sum increase normally takes effect for claims only after 3 months; the listed accident consequences are excepted.
The pre-contractual summary separately mentions a 6-month cancer wait; the child-specific conditions state 3 months. Confirm the applicable cancer period with the insurer.
childCriticalIllness.exclusions:
Death caused by the critical illness within 30 days of diagnosis, except cancer.
Congenital defects; HIV or AIDS.
The listed pre-existing tumours, conditions and diagnostic consultations; an exception requires no disease found or recovery after remission, written medical evidence and informed acceptance by the insurer.
War and radiation (except consequences of radiotherapy); causally related alcohol or drug effects; unlawful acts, intentional self-harm or attempted suicide.
Professional or extreme sport/leisure unless expressly accepted in the contract; the accident cover’s under-18 sport exception does not apply here.
childCriticalIllness.references: 028-05 §§2–6, appendix 1; printed pp. 61–67. General terms and pre-contractual information also apply.

disability.product: Visiško darbingumo netekimo draudimas (special conditions No. 028-06)
disability.summary: A payout on an irreversible loss of capacity for work due to illness or an accident.
disability.event:
An irreversible loss of capacity for work, where a capacity level of 0–25 % is established and the incapacity lasts continuously for at least 12 months.
The impairment must arise during cover and completely prevent income-producing work; the insurer decides whether the event meets the definition.
disability.payout:
The sum insured in force on the day of the event – to the insured person.
The cover ends after the payout.
disability.terms:
Aged 18 to 64 at the start; the cover lasts until the age of 65 at most.
Waiting period – 6 months (3 months for employee group insurance); not applied in the case of an accident.
Minimum sum insured – 10 000 EUR.
A sum increase is subject to the same 6-month (employee groups: 3-month) restriction, except incapacity caused by an insured accident. Written agreement or uninterrupted continuation of equivalent ERGO cover can waive the initial restriction.
disability.exclusions:
Acts of war, peacekeeping missions, combat duties, nuclear energy and radioactive radiation.
Effects of alcohol, narcotic or psychotropic substances.
Criminal acts; intentional self-harm or attempted suicide.
Professional and extreme sport or leisure unless the insurer accepted this risk in the contract.
HIV or AIDS.
The radioactive-radiation exclusion excepts the consequences of radiotherapy.
disability.references: 028-06 §§2–6; printed pp. 68–70. General terms and pre-contractual information also apply.

accidentDisability.product: Negalia dėl nelaimingo atsitikimo (special conditions No. 028-03, table No. 1)
accidentDisability.summary: A payout for long-term or permanent consequences of an accident – as a percentage of the disability sum insured.
accidentDisability.event: Injuries sustained in an accident that cause a long-term or permanent loss of some functions; also lasting effects of tick-borne encephalitis or Lyme disease.
accidentDisability.payout:
A share of the disability sum insured according to table No. 1, for example: paralysis of all limbs or irreversible coma – 100 %, paralysis of the lower limbs with pelvic organ dysfunction – 70 %, paralysis of one side of the body – 50 %.
The payout is increased by 15 % when the dominant arm is injured.
Payouts for one event within an insurance year – no more than 100 % of the sum.
Disability is normally assessed no sooner than 9 months after the event; the certificate must be issued within 18 months (24 for tick-borne diseases).
Only the most severe injury to the same body part is paid; organ benefits cannot exceed the amount for loss of that organ. Pre-existing loss of function is deducted. Following surgery, assessment is normally at least 6 months after surgery and 9 months after the accident; clearly irreversible loss may be paid earlier.
For the central nervous system examples in table 1, at least two signs from the relevant group are required. A benefit under that section cannot be combined with the specified trunk/limb bone benefits from the same external cause.
accidentDisability.terms:
Aged 0 to 69 at the start of the insurance.
Valid around the clock, worldwide.
accidentDisability.exclusions:
Intentional self-harm or attempted suicide.
Acts incurring criminal or administrative liability.
Narcotic or psychotropic substances; illnesses that cause seizures.
Acts of war, riots, nuclear energy and radiation; consequences of treatment not required by the accident.
Professional and extreme sport or leisure unless agreed otherwise (does not apply under 18).
Moderate/severe intoxication excludes an accident only when it influenced the event; poisoning by alcohol or the other specified substances is separately excluded.
accidentDisability.references: 028-03 §4.2, table 1 §§1–3; printed pp. 22, 28–39. General terms and pre-contractual information also apply.

injuries.product: Traumos dėl nelaimingo atsitikimo (special conditions No. 028-03, table No. 2)
injuries.summary: A payout for fractures, dislocations, soft tissue injuries, burns and poisoning – as a percentage of the injury sum insured.
injuries.event: A bone fracture, dislocation or subluxation, soft tissue injury or accidental acute poisoning sustained in an accident; the table also includes insect stings, tick-borne encephalitis and Lyme disease, and loss of pregnancy.
injuries.payout:
A percentage of the injury sum insured according to table No. 2, for example: fracture of the femoral head or neck – 14 %, humerus fracture – 9 %, Achilles tendon rupture – 5 %, nasal bone fracture – 3 %, ligament sprain – 1 %.
Increased by 50 % when osteosynthesis surgery is performed for an open fracture or to fix bone fragments (once per event), and for facial wounds. Increased by 100 % for an artificial joint implanted in the acute phase because of a joint fracture, or an injury during a confirmed pregnancy, excluding the pregnancy-loss benefit.
A second fracture at the callus/fixation site or second tear of the same meniscus, ligament, tendon or muscle is reduced by 50 %; later repetitions are not paid. Subluxation and the second dislocation are paid at 50 %, later dislocations are not paid. Partial tears and injuries in limbs with degenerative changes are reduced by 50 %; other table reductions also apply.
Payouts for one event – no more than 100 % of the sum.
Multiple breaks of one bone count once. Dislocation and soft-tissue injuries in the same limb are paid under the highest applicable item, not added together. Diagnostic evidence and individual table limits apply.
Pregnancy loss: 20 % for traumatic loss of a pregnancy longer than 22 weeks; 10 % for loss from other causes from week 14, paid once during the contract.
The 5 % Achilles-tendon example is without surgery; with surgery the table gives 7 %. A repeated sprain of the same joint within one year of the previous event is not paid.
injuries.terms:
Aged 0 to 69 at the start of the insurance.
Valid around the clock, worldwide.
Tick-borne encephalitis/Lyme disease under table 2 requires serological confirmation and first symptoms no earlier than 30 days after cover starts.
injuries.exclusions:
Attempted suicide, self-harm; taking part in a fight; criminal or administrative offences.
Pathological fractures, intervertebral disc damage and hernias; dental damage while eating.
Dislocations where the first dislocation happened before the cover started; fractures of osteosynthesis hardware and prostheses.
Narcotic substances; acts of war, radiation.
Professional and extreme sport or leisure unless agreed otherwise (does not apply under 18).
The fighting exclusion excepts necessary self-defence, performance of official duties and other socially valuable actions.
Moderate/severe intoxication excludes an accident only when it influenced the event; poisoning by alcohol or the other specified substances is separately excluded.
injuries.references: 028-03 §4.3, table 2; printed pp. 22–23, 40–47. General terms and pre-contractual information also apply.

dailyAllowance.summary: A chosen amount for every day of temporary incapacity for work after an accident.
dailyAllowance.event: Temporary incapacity for work caused by an accident recognised as an insured event, confirmed by a sick leave certificate; also when a parent who is insured for the daily allowance risk under the same contract gets a sick leave certificate to nurse an injured insured child.
dailyAllowance.payout:
The daily amount stated in the policy, paid from the first day of incapacity.
For no more than 30 days per event and 100 days per insurance year.
For injuries not listed in the injury table – for no more than 14 days.
dailyAllowance.terms: Aged 0 to 69 at the start, as for the other accident risks.
dailyAllowance.exclusions:
Incapacity not confirmed by a properly issued sick leave certificate.
The general exclusions of the accident insurance apply.
dailyAllowance.references: 028-03 §4.6; printed pp. 24–25. General terms and pre-contractual information also apply.

hospitalAllowance.summary: A chosen amount for every day of inpatient treatment.
hospitalAllowance.event:
Inpatient treatment because of an insured event under the disability, injury or additional assistance tables; also when an injured insured child is nursed in hospital by a parent who is insured for the hospital allowance risk under the same contract.
For a parent’s hospital stay, the child’s doctor must confirm the need for the parent’s presence, or the parent must document paying for their own bed-days. The cover can include the listed acute illnesses under table 3, not just accidental injuries.
hospitalAllowance.payout:
The daily amount stated in the policy, paid from the first day in hospital.
For no more than 30 days per event and 100 days per insurance year.
hospitalAllowance.terms: Aged 0 to 69 at the start, as for the other accident risks.
hospitalAllowance.exclusions:
Inpatient treatment for reasons not listed in the payout tables.
The general exclusions of the accident insurance apply.
hospitalAllowance.references: 028-03 §4.7; printed p. 25. General terms and pre-contractual information also apply.

medicalExpenses.product: Įprastinė medicininė pagalba, papildoma pagalba ir papildomos išlaidos (special conditions No. 028-03, table No. 3)
medicalExpenses.summary: Costs incurred after an accident are reimbursed against invoices, and fixed payouts are made for certain acute illnesses.
medicalExpenses.event:
Regular medical assistance requires all three accident risks: death, disability and injuries. Cosmetic surgery must take place within 5 years of the accident.
Additional assistance covers the listed accident expenses used within 5 years; listed acute illnesses must not have been diagnosed before this cover started and require hospitalisation and/or medical confirmation. Additional-expense reimbursement depends on what the policy expressly includes.
medicalExpenses.payout:
Regular medical assistance: up to 1 500 EUR for cosmetic plastic surgery, up to 1 000 EUR for rehabilitation and prosthetics, up to 1 000 EUR for psychological help (the last two with a disability of at least 15 %).
Additional assistance: search and rescue – up to 10 000 EUR, home adaptation and funeral – up to 600 EUR, psychologist – up to 300 EUR, transport, orthopaedic aids and diagnostic tests – up to 200 EUR per year.
Acute illnesses (appendicitis, sepsis, tick-borne encephalitis, type 1 diabetes and others) – 500 EUR per event, no more than 1 000 EUR per year.
All additional assistance payouts for one event together cannot exceed the additional assistance sum insured stated in the policy.
Additional expenses – within the sum agreed in the contract.
Table 3 also includes repatriation of the body or necessary funeral costs abroad within the 10 000 EUR entry limit, and wound stitching/dressings/injections/infusions up to 100 EUR per insurance year. Home adaptation and funeral/cremation each have a 600 EUR per-event limit; psychological help has a 300 EUR annual limit. The 200 EUR annual limits are separate for each listed transport, aid or diagnostic category.
Regular rehabilitation/prosthetics pays only costs not reimbursed elsewhere (or the unreimbursed part); rehabilitation includes the specified physiotherapy, exercise therapy and 10 massage sessions.
medicalExpenses.terms:
Aged 0 to 69 at the start of the insurance.
The insurer's approval is needed before using the regular medical assistance.
A 30-day waiting period applies to the acute illnesses in table 3 items 2.8–2.16, including tick-borne encephalitis and type 1 diabetes; it does not apply to every illness in the table.
medicalExpenses.exclusions:
Costs not supported by invoices or purchase documents.
Under table 3’s diagnostic-test item, doctor consultations are not reimbursed; the separate psychological-help benefit is subject to its own conditions.
Costs above those actually incurred when several contracts are in force.
The general exclusions of the accident insurance apply.
medicalExpenses.references: 028-03 §§4.4–4.5, 4.8, table 3; printed pp. 23–26, 48–49. General terms and pre-contractual information also apply.
